title: Telemetry lifecycle shepherding: field-blinding policy and audit hooks
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Observability pipelines currently retain raw instrumentation and trace attributes that may include sensitive customer or tenant-specific identifiers. Without a policy-first approach, we risk over-retention, complex redaction logic duplicated across services, and gaps in access provenance.

Goal: Implement a unified 'field-blinding' policy and audit hook system that minimizes PII captured in traces/logs/metrics while preserving debuggability. Provide tenant-scoped retention profiles, deterministic masking for debugable identifiers, and an access-provenance audit trail for observability reads. Ship as a platform-level capability with a config-driven rollout and monitoring.

Out of scope: full search-index encryption, downstream SSO entitlement sync (tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: Field-blinding library (Go/Python/Node) implemented and published to internal packages
Pipeline operators apply policies and redact or obfuscate configured fields without dropping trace/span linkage
Access events for observability reads (logs/traces/dashboards) are emitted to audit-log stream with tenant/context and persisted for 90 days by default
Retention profiles configurable per-tenant via Console and respected by archival/eraser jobs
E2E test that injects known PII patterns and verifies blinding, deterministic pseudonyms, and no raw PII in retention tier
Performance regression <5% p95 latency on traced request path with blinding enabled (compared to baseline)
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Design API for field-blinding rules (glob patterns, JSONPath, regex, type hints) and deterministic pseudonymization using per-tenant salt
Phase 1a: Tracing hooks to annotate spans with 'blind-safe'/'blind-unsafe' flags so runtime can decide to scrub or preserve minimal context
Phase 2: Integrate blinding runtime into metrics/log pipeline processors (fluentd/fluent-bit replacement operators) and tracing aggregator
Phase 3: Console UI for retention profile editing, default templates for compliance tiers (dev, standard, regulated)
Phase 4: Audit ingestion: every Console/dashboard or logs/traces query emits an access event with actor, scope, query-hash, and justification if high-risk fields requested
Trade-offs considered: full field removal reduces blast radius but impedes debugging; pseudonymization strikes balance but adds key-management needs (KMS integration already planned)
We will prefer deterministic pseudonyms for IDs so correlating events across systems remains possible while preventing reconstruction of raw identifiers

risks: Performance: regex-heavy rules can increase CPU usage in hot pipelines; mitigation: compile rules to efficient matchers and provide sampling knobs
False negatives: novel PII patterns may slip through; mitigation: allow user-defined hygiene rules + periodic regex healthchecks using synthetic corpora
Operator compatibility: some downstream consumers expect original fields; migration must include compatibility flag and rollback path
Compliance keys: deterministic pseudonyms require key management; delaying KMS integration reduces guarantees for regulated tenants
